purpose: Source-level licence inventory for the public-artifact safety audit.
assessment_scope: Permission to redistribute cached article text in a public repository. Short quotations and statutory exceptions require a separate assessment; the user's 15-word excerpt cap remains binding for all sources.
disclaimer: This inventory supports publication review and does not provide legal clearance.
source_discovery: Corpus manifest source IDs matched against the working-tree contents of git ls-files --cached -- docs results. The set includes metadata-only references; the content scanner determines which files actually embed source text.
evidence_method: Explicit licence elements were read from previously cached Europe PMC fullTextXML response bytes. Sources without those elements were checked against publisher or PMC pages. ResearchGate availability, PMC inclusion, free access, and local possession were not treated as redistribution permission.
limitations: Third-party figure, table, and other material rights were not individually reviewed.
Sources referenced only by author/title without a corpus source ID can be absent from this source-ID inventory; reconcile with the content scanner.
Publisher access errors and missing article-specific licences remain explicit uncertainties.
The classification 'no' means no recorded permission under the located publisher terms; statutory exceptions and separate permissions were not adjudicated.

policy_evidence.finding: PMC availability alone does not grant reuse permission, and author manuscripts can lack licence notices.
CC BY 4.0 permits sharing and adaptation with attribution, licence links, and change notices.
CC BY-NC-ND restricts commercial use and redistribution of adaptations.
OUP standard-publication public redistribution generally requires permission.

coverage_followup.scope: A second pass inspected staged docs/results for DOI strings and author-year citations outside the original corpus-ID inventory.
limitations: The 517 LOTUS bibliography-only articles were not fetched or licensed individually; their article-text permission remains unassessed.
The source-level scanner separately verifies actual embedded quotations; metadata-only citations are not classified as article-body redistribution.
